subject: Hammerhead sharks
hook: HAMMERHEAD SHARKS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: A hammerhead shark's wide head does not drive its sharp underwater maneuvering—unusual vertebrae do—while the head's extreme eye placement grants the shark a full 360 degrees of vertical vision, letting it see above and below at all times.
angle_support: The shape of the head was previously thought to aid in close-quarters maneuverability, allowing sharp turning movement without losing stability. However, the unusual structure of its vertebrae instead has been found to be instrumental in making the turns correctly, more so than the shape of its head
The positioning of the eyes, mounted on the sides of the shark's distinctive hammer head, allows 360° of vision in the vertical plane, meaning the animals can see above and below them at all times.
title: The Real Reason Hammerheads Have Flat Heads
description: Most people think the hammerhead's wide head is for steering, but the truth lies in its skeleton. Learn how eye placement gives this shark a massive visual advantage.
narration: HAMMERHEAD SHARKS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture that wide, flat head acting like a steering rudder for tight ocean corners. But that wing-like head shape does not actually drive their agility. Unusual skeletal vertebrae, not the hammer's shape, actually drive their sharpest underwater maneuvers. Instead, the head’s real secret is optics. With eyes at the extreme ends, they possess a full circle of vertical vision. This ability lets them see everything directly above and beneath them simultaneously. This unique anatomy ensures they never have a vertical blind spot.
